title: Training-Free Guided Diffusion for Planning: A Unified Framework via Doob’s h-Transform with Safety Guarantees
claim: Increasing the inference-time rollout budget improves safety and task success, but latency grows sharply at the largest budget.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side; dual-metric line plot left, latency right; dashed line at chosen setting
description: Two side-by-side line plots share a title, 'Medium scenario family (16 tasks, 5 trials/task)', and an x-axis of PIC rollout budget L at 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256. The left panel plots rate (%) against L with error bars. A blue line with circles shows obstacle safety, rising from about 82 to 91 and then 89. A red line with squares shows task success, rising from about 51 to 84. A legend sits at the bottom left. The right panel plots warm latency in seconds, a purple line with circles that rises from about 5.3 s to 10.1 s and bends steeply upward at 256. Both panels have a vertical dashed line at L=256, which marks the default setting. Light grid lines run behind the data. The eye goes first to the diverging blue and red curves, then to the steep latency rise.

abstract: This paper studies the theoretical foundations of guidance mechanisms in continuous-time score-based diffusion models. We adopt Doob’s h-transform as a principled framework for characterizing ideal guided diffusion processes and analyze the discrepancy between ideal and approximate guidance. Our analysis provides explicit error bounds and yields probabilistic guarantees on satisfying prescribed constraints, which are particularly important for safety-critical planning. We further show that the Doob-based formulation induces a stochastic optimal control problem, enabling practical guidance design without additional model training. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on robotic navigation tasks, including language-conditioned planning.
